nodes.rationale: Established by direct test, not by reading the skill: the state is global but enforcement is per-session, because the PreToolUse hook is registered when freeze runs IN a session. nodes.label: Truncate-per-test isolation requires fileParallelism false
nodes.rationale: Vitest defaults fileParallelism to true. Two integration files truncating one shared DATABASE_URL race: one file's beforeEach TRUNCATE fires between another's commit and its read-back. An ok result with an empty read-back is a concurrency signature, not a data one.

nodes.label: Defect class: schema with no code path
nodes.norm_label: defect class: schema with no code path
nodes.rationale: Recurs because schema was designed in one pass against the whole spec while code arrives phase by phase, so 'the column exists' reads as 'the feature exists'. Rule: verify a prerequisite by finding the CODE PATH, not the schema object.

nodes.label: F6: tools written, typechecked, and never registered
nodes.norm_label: f6: tools written, typechecked, and never registered
nodes.rationale: The fifth instance of schema-with-no-code-path, in tool-layer form. complete_commitment and update_commitment compiled and had unit tests while absent from buildToolRegistry; the first symptom would have been a runtime 'unknown tool' on the one utterance Phase 3 exists to support.

nodes.label: listRecent ordering is undefined for a same-transaction batch
nodes.norm_label: listrecent ordering is undefined for a same-transaction batch
nodes.rationale: t_created defaults to now(), which in Postgres is TRANSACTION start time, so rows written in one transaction share a byte-identical timestamp and the id DESC tiebreak is arbitrary. Fixed in the test, not the schema: production writes the two messages in separate transactions.

nodes.label: registry.coverage.test.ts, the guard that closes F6
nodes.norm_label: registry.coverage.test.ts, the guard that closes f6
nodes.rationale: Scans the orchestrator SOURCE for emitted tool names rather than calling runTurn, because a call-based check would only cover branches the fixtures reach. Verified by mutation, and it caught attach_context automatically two commits later with no edit to the test.

nodes.label: The independent-review gate earns its cost
nodes.norm_label: the independent-review gate earns its cost
nodes.rationale: A read-only staff review found 11 issues, 3 confirmed blockers, while all 8 original unit tests passed. That is PHASE-1-DESIGN 4.3's warning happening in practice, and the strongest argument in this repo for the gate.

nodes.label: Four-stage orchestrator (Interpret, Resolve, Mutate, Respond)
nodes.rationale: Four stages because they have different failure modes and must be independently testable. Two cells of 3.1's table are PROHIBITIONS: Interpret never receives a database handle, Respond never receives one either.

nodes.label: The partial-commit rule
nodes.rationale: A partial commit is safe only if it is VISIBLE. Committable intents commit; blocked ones are asked about; the reply states both halves so the user can still say 'undo that'. If nothing is committable, no turn_id is minted at all.

nodes.label: Trace persistence on messages
nodes.rationale: An LLM failure with no trace is unfixable; a 200 OK can still be a wrong answer. Written even when the turn mutates nothing, because those are the turns worth studying, which is exactly why trace lives on messages and not on action_log, whose ledger has no row for a non-mutating turn.

nodes.label: turn_id originates inside executeTurn, never in the orchestrator
nodes.norm_label: turn_id originates inside executeturn, never in the orchestrator
nodes.rationale: Hoisting id generation into the orchestrator would change a Phase-1-owned CI-verified signature AND create a state the schema forbids: a turn_id on a message that appears in zero action_log rows. A turn that mutates nothing has turn_id NULL.

nodes.label: Three-tier time model
nodes.rationale: Spec 18 conflates a timestamp ('in two hours') with an event trigger ('after Arun replies'). Building them as one type produces reminders that fire at invented times. Split into deterministic, relational, and event_trigger tiers.

nodes.label: Early completion must not fire the rule
nodes.norm_label: early completion must not fire the rule
nodes.rationale: The correctness requirement of the whole section, satisfied structurally: evaluation reads LIVE state at evaluate_at. Zero rows (an invalidated subject) also means DO NOT FIRE; reading it as 'not completed, therefore fire' would remind the user about a commitment that no longer exists.

nodes.label: fired_at is the idempotency key
nodes.rationale: Delivery is at-least-once; fired_at collapses it to effectively-once. The redundant fired_at IS NULL guard costs nothing and makes a double-fire impossible even if the row lock were somehow not held. pg_cron would have needed the identical guard.

nodes.label: In-process reminder poller with an injected clock
nodes.norm_label: in-process reminder poller with an injected clock
nodes.rationale: pg_cron is absent from pgvector/pgvector:pg17 and the custom-image path needs GHCR publish rights the team lacks. The clock is a parameter because testTimeout is 15s and the poll interval is 30s, so any test that waits for a real tick times out having proved nothing.

nodes.label: A clock tick is not undoable (invariant 4)
nodes.norm_label: a clock tick is not undoable (invariant 4)
nodes.rationale: undoTurn filters actor_kind user_turn, so a scheduled_job turn returns zero rows and throws TurnNotFoundError. Access control is the filter, not a lie in the tool metadata: fire_reminder still declares invertibility full because firing IS reversible.

nodes.label: The LLM never computes a timestamp
nodes.norm_label: the llm never computes a timestamp
nodes.rationale: Date arithmetic across DST is the canonical 'different result each run' case, which belongs in a script. The model extracts the verbatim phrase; chrono-node resolves it deterministically from (text, instant, timezone).

nodes.label: Recursive schemas unsupported; flatten conditional rules
nodes.norm_label: recursive schemas unsupported; flatten conditional rules
nodes.rationale: Anthropic structured outputs do not support recursive schemas under the strict subset. A shape the model cannot emit is a shape we must not store, so spec 25's conditional workflows are flattened to a fixed depth.

nodes.label: Lateness is derived in the tool layer
nodes.norm_label: lateness is derived in the tool layer
nodes.rationale: Derived from two timestamptz columns inside complete_commitment, never from model output and never in packages/db. Both are absolute instants, so the difference is zone- and DST-independent by construction. A null expectedAt means null lateness, never zero.

nodes.label: Conditional rules evaluate at the deadline, never continuously
nodes.norm_label: conditional rules evaluate at the deadline, never continuously
nodes.rationale: 'If Arun hasn't sent the schema BY FRIDAY' is a statement about Friday, not Wednesday. Continuous evaluation fires on Wednesday when Arun simply has not gotten to it, which is spec 26's nagging. A database trigger was also rejected: it writes state with no actor.

nodes.label: The demo endpoint
nodes.rationale: A real DX defect: with no UI until Phase 5, every section 5 judgement is unfalsifiable by a test suite. Three guards: off by default, loopback-only, key required at startup. A demo CLI was rejected as a second entry point that would drift from server.ts's bootstrap.

nodes.label: Definition of done for every feature
nodes.norm_label: definition of done for every feature
nodes.rationale: Five steps in order: tests green, review clean, graphify update run, GRAPH_REPORT reviewed, committed and pushed.

nodes.label: Standing caveat: no recorded model output exists
nodes.norm_label: standing caveat: no recorded model output exists
nodes.rationale: The live eval lane (69 paid calls, manual) has never been run. Phase 3 adds a SECOND model call, so the unmeasured surface grew. The mandatory template fallback makes a Respond failure cosmetic, which is a mitigation, not evidence.

nodes.label: Public-repo hygiene rules
nodes.rationale: Never commit secrets; never put real names, emails, or personal data of actual team members in code, fixtures, or tests. Use the spec's fictional names instead.

nodes.label: README Barkha demo walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Three curls walking create, complete-late, and undo, plus an explanation of why the completion takes two turns so the ask does not read as a rough edge.

nodes.label: One Haiku call with a mandatory template fallback
nodes.norm_label: one haiku call with a mandatory template fallback
nodes.rationale: No tools and no DB handle, so a hallucination produces a wrong sentence and never a wrong row. The fallback is mandatory because the mutation has ALREADY committed, so a cosmetic model failure must not 500. Templating alone fails 20's optional late prompt and 30's 'Karthik from Hult?'.

nodes.label: The auto_match band is near-unreachable by construction
nodes.norm_label: the auto_match band is near-unreachable by construction
nodes.rationale: Auto-match needs identical content-token sets; one extra token caps a two-token match at 0.900, under the 0.92 threshold. So the demo's completion ASKS, and that is spec 27 working. A threshold band unreachable by construction is a documentation defect even when every line of code is correct.

nodes.label: One inverse handler per table, dispatching on patch shape
nodes.norm_label: one inverse handler per table, dispatching on patch shape
nodes.rationale: registerInverseHandler throws on a duplicate table key, so two tools registering for one table is a startup crash. Re-keying by tool name was rejected: undoTurn reads target_table and never passes tool_name, and coupling undo to names would orphan historical action_log rows on a rename.

nodes.label: Three-band entity resolution with hard vetoes
nodes.norm_label: three-band entity resolution with hard vetoes
nodes.rationale: Never a single cosine cutoff and never transitive closure: a published benchmark showed transitivity collapsed Pair-F1 from 0.540 to 0.000, because one false-positive link silently merges unrelated entities. Hard vetoes on owner/recipient/status raised cluster purity 51.6% to 84.4%.

nodes.label: LLM proposes, backend validates and commits
nodes.norm_label: llm proposes, backend validates and commits
nodes.rationale: Spec 37. Full write power through typed validated tools, never raw SQL from model output. This closes the injection path: ingested content saying 'delete all commitments' produces at most a proposed call that validation rejects.

nodes.label: A wrong merge is worse than a duplicate
nodes.norm_label: a wrong merge is worse than a duplicate
nodes.rationale: Spec 23 (avoid duplicates) and 7 (ownership matters) cannot both be optimised by one threshold. Resolved: a wrong merge silently destroys a commitment; a duplicate is visible and correctable by saying 'those are the same thing'. Bias toward splitting; ask in the ambiguous band.

nodes.label: Bitemporal data model (invalidate, never delete)
nodes.rationale: Vendor memory benchmarks (Zep vs Mem0) publicly contradict each other, so the design was borrowed rather than the dependency. Graphiti defaults to Neo4j, adding a second datastore for no capability that cannot be written in a migration. Four timestamps: t_valid, t_invalid, t_created, t_expired.

nodes.label: One Postgres, no separate vector store
nodes.norm_label: one postgres, no separate vector store
nodes.rationale: The deciding argument is transactional, not performance: a separate vector database would let an embedding write succeed while the corresponding commitment write fails.

nodes.label: commitment_notes is a table, not a column (finding F4)
nodes.norm_label: commitment_notes is a table, not a column (finding f4)
nodes.rationale: A notes column would be overwritten by the second piece of context and would carry no provenance. Spec 20's 'do not make judgmental statements' is only auditable if the source message is recoverable. One commitment accumulates many notes: a one-to-many is a table.
